candidates.claim: fw-01 enables telnet management access on the ot interface from 10.10.10.0/24, which violates the registry rule that telnet must not be enabled anywhere and that device management is allowed only from MGMT 10.10.99.0/24 on the mgmt interface.
candidates.remediation: Remove the telnet management line on fw-01 and restrict any remaining management access to MGMT 10.10.99.0/24 on the mgmt interface.

candidates.claim: The baseline delta records that a global telnet line for 10.10.10.0 was added on fw-01 and is not present in the approved baseline.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile this deviation: remove the added telnet line or document an approved exception.

candidates.claim: fw-01 has the asa_http_server global setting enabled; the registry bans IOS HTTP/HTTPS servers but does not state whether the ASA HTTP server must be disabled, so compliance cannot be determined from the registry.

sw-core-01 trunks Gi1/0/22 and Gi1/0/24 carry VLAN 10, while the rule says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10; the approved trunk table permits VLAN 10 on these trunks, so the intent is ambiguous for core uplinks.

clarifications.question: Does the registry's ban on IOS HTTP/HTTPS servers also cover the ASA HTTP server on fw-01 (global asa_http_server enabled at fw-01:109), or is only HTTPS/ASDM management from MGMT on the mgmt interface required?

The rule says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10, but the approved trunk table allows VLAN 10 on sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 and Gi1/0/24 (lines sw-core-01:175 and sw-core-01:187). Are these core trunks an approved exception to the OT-facing-only rule?
